reasoning_content:
Alright, now I've got the whole picture of install.sh:

1. Non-interactive mode via the `QISUTU_INSTALL_LANGUAGE` environment variable.
2. The instance name is derived from the directory name. `/opt/qisutu` is recommended.
3. On Ubuntu, it installs apache2, perl, mariadb-server, etc. via apt.
4. It creates a runtime user `qisutu`, an Apache config, and a systemd service.
5. It creates a temporary bootstrap DB user.
6. It enables the DB service and the install-complete path unit, and restarts apache.
7. After that, I need to run the web installer at `http://HOST/qisutu/install.pl`.

The tricky part: the web installer (install.pl) is a browser-based wizard. I'll need to operate it with curl in non-interactive mode. Let me look at the web installer to see what steps are involved and whether it's scriptable.

Important: the task states that the repository has been checked out to `/workspace`. According to the guide, each instance needs its own main directory, and the directory name becomes the instance ID. The recommended path is `/opt/qisutu`. So I should copy the repo to `/opt/qisutu` and run `./install.sh` there.

Also, I'll need to check whether systemd is available in this container. Since this is a Docker container, systemd might not be running. Let me verify. If systemd isn't available, `systemctl` commands will fail, and since install.sh has `set -euo pipefail`, the installation will fail. Hmm, but maybe this container has systemd running as PID 1. Let me check.

Let me look at the web installer and figure out how to operate it.

action.command: ps -p 1 -o comm=; systemctl is-system-running 2>&1 | head -2; ls /run/systemd/system 2>&1 | head -3; which apt-get curl perl mariadb mysql apache2 2>&1
